prerequisites: Mechanics (kinetics, statics and dynamics) in the surface and in space
To solve regular linear differential comparisons with constant coefficients

learning_outcomes.text: The student is able to select an appropriate system for motion or force transmission (linkage mechanism or cam–follower mechanism) and design this system from both a kinematic and dynamic perspective.
The student can select and apply procedures for the analysis and synthesis of mechanisms in both 2D and 3D.

The student is able to select suitable motion profiles for cam–follower systems or servo-driven actuators, while taking into account the vibration phenomena caused by these motion profiles in flexible follower systems.
The student is able to formulate and solve the dynamic equations for linear vibration problems.
The student can assess vibration-related problems, and can propose and develop vibration suppression measures.
The student is able to use numerical tools (MATLAB) for the kinematic and dynamic analysis of mechanisms and for analyzing simplified models of complex vibration problems.
The student can verify the obtained solutions and results through validation calculations and critically evaluate them based on physical insight and technological constraints.
The student can independently perform and report these numerical analyses in a clear and well-structured report.
The role of kinematic and dynamic analysis and synthesis in machine design.
Procedures for mechanism analysis and synthesis.
Familiarity with commonly used elements and systems for motion or force transmission, with emphasis on linkage mechanisms and cam–follower mechanisms.

Design of motion profiles (for cam–follower systems or servo-driven actuators), with special attention to the dynamic phenomena caused by motion in flexible follower systems (i.e., the connection with vibration analysis).
Fundamental equations, common terminology, the effects of mechanical vibrations on humans and machines, procedures for analysis and synthesis, and principles of vibration suppression.
Applying techniques known from the Mechanics course for the kinematic and dynamic analysis of machine mechanisms (primarily planar mechanisms).
Using computer-aided tools for kinematic and dynamic calculations and for dynamic simulation (Applied Motion, MATLAB), including time-domain simulation of a nonlinear system.
Formulating a design problem as an optimization problem.

Formulating and solving the dynamic equilibrium equations for linear vibration problems; designing vibration-reduction measures; assessing vibration problems (disturbance and risk); using numerical tools (MATLAB); and employing simplified models for complex vibration problems.
A critical and creative mindset, including during the analysis of existing mechanisms: Is this optimal? How could it be improved?
Critical interpretation of computer-generated results based on physical insight.
Attention to physical interpretation and technological constraints.
Attention to units and dimensional consistency.
Attention to clear and effective reporting.

syllabus_topics: Study of rod and ridge mechanisms
Speed, acceleration and power analysis of machines
Introductions to computer-supported kinematic and dynamic analysis
Design of motion trajectories (for ridge/follower systems or servo-controlled drives)
Dynamic phenomena caused by motion in flexible follower systems
Introduction – examples of vibrations in machines and vehicles
Single-degree-of-freedom systems (forced response under harmonic excitation)
Single-degree-of-freedom systems (forced response under random excitation)
Multi-degree-of-freedom systems (free response, forced response, modal transformation)
Vibration isolation and vibration suppression: design aspects – effects of vibrations on humans
Vibrations in rotating machinery and internal combustion engines – imbalance and balancing techniques

assessment_methods.method: Assignments (kinematic and dynamic analysis of a mechanism)
Oral exam with written preparation (Mechanical Vibrations)

assessment_rules: The marks on both parts (Motion and Mechanical Vibrations) will be added together with equal weight. If the mark on one or both parts is less than 10/20, the total mark is rounded down. If the mark on one part is less than 8 on 20, the total mark will be limited to 9/20. For a resit, students will revise their work and have a second evaluating conversation.
bibliography: R.L. Norton, Design of machinery. An introduction to the synthesis and analysis of mechanisms and machines, McGraw-Hill, 3rd edition, 2004
H.H. Mabie & C.F. Reinholtz, Mechanisms and dynamics of machinery
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
